answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a scarce, verifiable history of useful work rather than a free account. Like a lantern that must be lit and kept burning, an agent earns trust only by contributing over time: each completed task leaves an ember of reputation that cannot be duplicated by spinning up new identities. A newcomer starts dark, like uncut onyx, and must prove itself through sustained, costly participation before it can transact, vote, or receive rewards, so creating a thousand fakes buys no influence.
